construction_markdown:
No leaderboard code is submitted. I investigated the natural degree-65 deformation of the Reed–Solomon–affine construction.

Use the campaign field `F = F_2[Z]/(Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1)`, its 15-dimensional additive subspace `A = span_F2{1,alpha,...,alpha^14}`, and the affine truth-table inner map `H(z)_y = z_0 + sum_{i=1}^{15} z_i y_i`. For a binary subspace `W <= F^2`, define

`M_W = {sum_{j=0}^{65} c_j X^j : c_0,...,c_63 in F and (c_65,c_64) in W}`

and concatenate evaluation on `A` with `H`. Its dimension is `1024 + dim_F2(W)`. The proved obstruction says that `dim(W) >= 17`, and hence every attempted dimension at least 1041 in this family, necessarily introduces a word of weight 535,805,952, which is 16,384 below the target. Thus this entire top-two-coefficient swap mechanism cannot improve the 1040-dimensional degree-at-most-64 boundary.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Reusable lemma for the combinatorial architecture and proof positions: for every `c in F_{2^16}^*` and every additive subgroup `A` of size 32768, there is a 65-subset `S <= A` such that `sum S = 0` and `c product_{s in S}(x-s) != 1` for all `x in A\S`. The proof is the fixed-scale incidence bound followed by the impossible Steiner system `S(64,65,32767)`; translation enforces zero root sum without changing the avoided-value property.
discussion_posts.subject: Fixed-scale 65-root avoidance with zero root sum

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Obstruction for the construction architect and finite-parameter optimizer: retaining all coefficients through degree 63 and replacing the two degree-64/65 coefficient spaces by any binary `W <= F^2` cannot exceed dimension 1040 at the required distance. If `dim W >= 17`, dimension intersection forces `(c,0) in W`, and the avoidance lemma supplies a codeword of weight exactly 535,805,952.
discussion_posts.subject: Top-two coefficient swaps cannot reach dimension 1041

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Question for the next construction-component investigator or bottleneck breaker: if degrees 0 through 62 remain free and `W <= F^3` controls `(c_65,c_64,c_63)`, dimension 1041 requires `dim W >= 33`, forcing a nonzero `(c,0,0) in W`. Can one prove a fixed-scale avoidance lemma with both `e_1(S)=0` and `e_2(S)=0`? Translation kills `e_1` and leaves `e_2` invariant because 64 and `binom(65,2)=2080` are even. Such a lemma would close the top-three coefficient frontier; an explicit counterexample could instead identify a viable escape.

distance_audit: The affine inner word has weight 0 at symbol 0, weight 32768 at symbol 1, and weight 16384 at every other nonzero field symbol.
The constructed obstruction polynomial has exactly 65 roots in `A` and takes neither value 0 nor value 1 at the other 32703 evaluation points.
Its concatenated weight is therefore `32703 times 16384 = 535,805,952`.
The required distance is 535,822,336, so the word is short by exactly 16,384. A single such nonzero word proves that the family member fails the distance requirement.
The argument works for every binary subspace `W` of dimension at least 17; it does not rely on sampling or an average-distance assertion.
explicitness_audit: For every symbolically specified `W`, the family has a deterministic full-generator-matrix algorithm using a reduced-row-echelon binary basis of `W`.
Coordinates are ordered lexicographically by the 15-bit descriptions of `a in A` and `y in F_2^15`; field arithmetic uses the fixed degree-16 modulus.
The generator algorithm performs polynomially many fixed-degree field and bit operations and emits all matrix entries.
The incidence argument is existential only in order to exhibit a forbidden low-weight codeword. It is used as a negative distance proof, not as a hidden construction or selector.
No qualifying code with dimension above 1040 is claimed, so this handoff is not a leaderboard submission and does not trigger publication or records validation.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Given an explicit binary basis `(u_r,v_r)` of `W`, first put it in deterministic reduced row-echelon order. Emit rows indexed by `(j,i)` for `0 <= j <= 63`, `0 <= i <= 15`, corresponding to `alpha^i X^j`, followed by one row for each basis pair, corresponding to `u_r X^65 + v_r X^64`. For every lexicographically ordered coordinate `(a,y) in A times F_2^15`, evaluate the row polynomial at `a`, expand the value in the fixed basis `(1,alpha,...,alpha^15)`, and output its affine truth-table bit at `y`. This generates the investigated family; it is not asserted to meet the target when `dim W >= 17`.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: At most `O(65 k n poly(16))` bit operations and `k n` output bits, where `k = 1024 + dim(W) <= 1056`; hence `O(n)` for the fixed field and degree, and in particular `n^{O(1)}`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: There are exactly `k n` entries. Each entry requires evaluation of a degree-at-most-65 polynomial over the fixed 16-bit field and one 15-variable affine-form evaluation. Gaussian elimination on the at-most-32-dimensional input basis costs only `O(32^3)` bit operations. Thus the stated bound includes every emitted entry and is polynomial in `n`.

The theorem does not cover top-three or wider coefficient trades, outer spaces that sacrifice some lower coefficients, different additive evaluation sets, or non-affine inner codes.

proof_markdown:
### Proposition

Let `F`, `A`, and `H` be as above. For a binary subspace `W <= F^2`, let `C_W` be the concatenated evaluation code generated by polynomials whose coefficients through degree 63 are unrestricted and whose pair `(c_65,c_64)` lies in `W`. If `C_W` has minimum distance at least 535,822,336, then `dim_F2(W) <= 16` and `dim_F2(C_W) <= 1040`.

### Dimension

The polynomial space has binary dimension `64·16 + dim(W)`. A nonzero polynomial of degree at most 65 cannot vanish at every point of the 32768-element set `A`, so outer evaluation is injective. The affine truth-table map is also injective. Hence `dim(C_W)=1024+dim(W)`.

Suppose `dim(W)>=17`. Inside the 32-dimensional binary space `F^2`, the subspace `F×{0}` has dimension 16. Therefore

`dim(W intersect (F×{0})) >= dim(W)+16-32 >= 1`.

Choose `(c,0)` in this intersection with `c != 0`.

### Fixed-scale avoidance lemma

For every such `c`, there is a 65-subset `S` of `A` satisfying

`c product_{s in S}(x-s) != 1` for every `x in A\S`.

For a fixed `x`, translation sends a 65-subset `S` avoiding `x` to a 65-subset `T=S+x` of `A\{0}`, and the displayed equality becomes `product_{t in T}t=c^-1`. Let `M_c` be the number of such `T`. Count pairs `(T,R)` with `R` a 64-subset of `T`. There are `65M_c` pairs. Conversely, a given 64-subset `R` has at most one extension because its missing element would have to be

`z = c^-1 / product_{r in R} r`.

Thus `65M_c <= binom(32767,64)`. If every 65-subset `S` had at least one covering point `x`, the number of incidences would satisfy

`binom(32768,65) <= 32768 M_c <= (32768/65) binom(32767,64) = binom(32768,65)`.

All inequalities would be equalities. In particular, every 64-subset of `A\{0}` would occur in exactly one qualifying 65-subset, producing a Steiner system `S(64,65,32767)`. Counting its blocks through a fixed 62-subset would require

`binom(32705,2) / binom(3,2)`

to be an integer. But `binom(32705,2)=534,792,160` is congruent to 1 modulo 3. This contradiction proves the lemma.

### Zero-sum normalization

Let `t=sum_{s in S}s` and replace `S` by `S+t`. Since 65 is odd and the characteristic is two, the translated root sum is `t+65t=0`. Translation permutes `A`, and

`product_{r in S+t}(x-r) = product_{s in S}((x+t)-s)`,

so the avoided-value property is unchanged. Write `G(X)=product_{s in S+t}(X-s)`. It is monic of degree 65 and its degree-64 coefficient is zero. Consequently `f=cG` has top pair `(c,0) in W`, and all its lower coefficients are permitted; hence `f` is a message in `M_W`.

### Forbidden weight

The polynomial `f` has exactly its 65 selected roots in `A`, and at every other point its value is nonzero and not equal to 1. All 32703 nonroot inner blocks therefore have weight 16384. The resulting nonzero codeword has weight

`(32768-65)·16384 = 535,805,952 < 535,822,336`.

Thus every `W` of dimension at least 17 fails the target. Contrapositively, a target-qualified member has `dim(W)<=16` and dimension at most 1040.

proof_steps.proof: There are 64 unrestricted coefficients in the 16-dimensional field and `dim(W)` binary degrees of freedom in the top pair. Degree-at-most-65 evaluation on 32768 distinct points and the affine inner map are injective.
The ambient binary dimension of `F^2` is 32, while `F×{0}` has dimension 16. The subspace-dimension inequality gives intersection dimension at least `dim(W)-16`.

The incidence count gives at most `binom(32768,65)` covered-set incidences. Universal coverage would force equality and hence a Steiner system `S(64,65,32767)`. Its blocks through a fixed 62-subset would number `binom(32705,2)/3`, impossible because the numerator is 1 modulo 3.
proof_steps.statement: For every nonzero `c`, some 65-subset `S` of `A` has `c product(x-s)!=1` at every unselected point.

proof_steps.proof: Translation by the root sum makes the new sum zero because 65 is odd in characteristic two. It permutes `A` and translates the argument of the root polynomial, preserving fixed-scale avoidance.
proof_steps.statement: The avoiding 65-set may additionally be chosen with root sum zero.

proof_steps.proof: Multiplying the normalized monic root polynomial by `c` gives top pair `(c,0) in W`. It has 65 zero symbols, no symbol 1, and 32703 nonzero non-one symbols, each producing inner weight 16384.
proof_steps.statement: Every `C_W` with `dim(W)>=17` contains a word of weight 535,805,952.

proof_steps.proof: The violating weight is 16,384 below the required distance. Therefore a qualifying member must have `dim(W)<=16`, and the dimension formula gives `k<=1040`.
proof_steps.statement: The investigated top-two-coefficient family cannot improve dimension 1040.

theorem_statement: In the exact `F_{2^16}` Reed–Solomon–affine setup, let all coefficients through degree 63 be unrestricted and constrain `(c_65,c_64)` to a binary subspace `W <= F^2`. If the resulting length-`2^30` binary code meets distance 535,822,336, then `dim_F2(W) <= 16` and its dimension is at most 1040. Indeed, every `W` of dimension at least 17 produces a codeword of weight exactly 535,805,952.
title: A 1040-dimensional ceiling for degree-65 top-two coefficient swaps
